JUDGMENT

This appeal is preferred by the appellant challenging Crl.Appeal No.2560/2019 the conviction judgment and order of sentence passed by the learned I ACMM, Bengaluru in C.C.No.30400/2015,
dated:16.11.2019 and prays to set aside the impugned judgment and to acquit the accused.
2. The appellant herein was the accused No.1 and respondent was the State before the trial court.
For the sake of convenience, parties would be referred to by the ranks they were assigned before the trial court.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:

sentences.text:
The accused has been charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 419,
420, 465, 468 and 471 r/w. Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 66, 66(C) and 66(d)
of Information Technology Act in C.C.No.30400/2015 (Crime No.360/2014 of Tilak Nagar Police Station, Bengaluru)

After filing the charge sheet, the charge has been framed against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 465,
468 and 471 r/w. Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 66, 66(C) and 66(D) of Information Technology Act.
The accused No.1 has pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
The case is posted for prosecution evidence.

After completion of the trial and on hearing the arguments, the learned Magistrate has hold guilty of Crl.Appeal No.2560/2019 the offences charged against the accused and was pleased to convict the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 465, 468 and 471 r/w. Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 66, 66(C) and 66(D) of Information Technology Act.
4.
The appellant/accused No.1 has preferred this appeal on the following grounds :

It is contended that the impugned judgment passed by the trial court is illegal,
perverse, arbitrary and without application of mind.
In the present case, C.Ws.1 to 4 have not been examined i.e., the complainant and C.W.3 who had paid the amount to the accused persons are not examined.
Hence there is no evidence regarding payment to the accused persons.
As such, the impugned judgment is illegal and shall be set aside.
Further the evidence of P.Ws.3 and 4 is not related to this case.

Their evidence is copies in the present case and they deposed the evidence of their case i.e.,
C.C.No.20412/2015 which is being challenged before the appellate court in Crl.
Appeal No.2536/2019 pending on the file of CCH No.61, Bengaluru.
The only connection given is that by seeing the e-mail sent to P.w.3, C.Ws.1 and 3 believed the accused persons and paid the amount as per the charge sheet.
But nothing is there in the evidence as related to this case in their evidence.
Hence their evidence has no use to convict Crl.Appeal No.2560/2019 the appellant.
C.Ws.1 to 4 have not been examined in this case.
No recovery has been made from the possession of the appellant.
The learned Magistrate has erred in convicting the appellant/accused even though there is no absolute proof of evidence against him.
The guilt of the appellant/accused is not proved beyond reasonable doubt.
The learned Magistrate has convicted the appellant on the basis of assumptions, in fact there is no proof regarding the payment of alleged amount to the accused.
Hence the appellant cannot be hold guilty of the offences charged against him.
No amount was seized from the accused.
Hence prayed to allow the appeal by setting aside the impugned judgment passed by the trial court.
5. On service of notice, the learned Public Prosecutor has appeared on behalf of the State.
6. The trial court records were secured.

7. Heard.

sentences.text:
The points raised for consideration are as under:
1.
Whether the appellant has made out sufficient grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and order of sentence passed by the trial court ?

Crl.Appeal No.2560/2019 2. Whether the appellant/accused has made out a ground to set off for the imprisonment already undergone by him in judicial custody ?
3.
What Order?

9. My findings to the above points are:
POINT No.1 : Negative, POINT No.2 : Affirmative, POINT No.3 : As per final order,
for the following:
REASONS 10. POINT Nos.1 & 2:- Since both these points are interconnected to each other, they have been taken up together for discussion in order to avoid the repetition of facts.
11.
I have considered the complaint averments, oral and documentary evidence placed before the trial court along with appeal averments placed before this court, the arguments addressed by both the sides.
12. It is the specific contention of the appellant that the evidence of P.Ws.3 and 4 is not pertaining to this case.
They have given evidence in C.C.No.20412/2015 which has been challenged in Crl. Appeal No.2536/2019 Crl.Appeal No.2560/2019 pending before CCH No.61.
The only connection is that e-mail is sent to P.W.3.
Hence on the basis of their evidence, the accused has been wrongly convicted by the learned Magistrate.
13. In view of the aforesaid contention, it is pertinent to refer to the evidence recorded by the learned Magistrate in C.C.No.30400/2015.
It is noted that P.W.3 is one Balakrishna and P.W4 is Dinesh Kumar,
The deposition is signed by the witnesses and the learned Magistrate.
On perusal of the deposition, there is nothing to establish that the evidence of the said witnesses are not pertaining to this case.
Even otherwise it is necessary to refer to the charge sheet wherein they are arrayed as C.Ws.5 and 6 respectively.
On considering the aforesaid evidence and the charge sheet, it can be safely said that the learned Magistrate has rightly examined the charge sheet witnesses.
There is nothing on record to prove that they are not the witnesses in this case.
Hence the contention taken by the appellant cannot be accepted.

14. In the present case, the victims are P.Ws.3 and 4, who are son and father & both of them have deposed in their evidence that the accused assured them to get admission to Belgaum Mecical Santhosh Rai Alias Santhosh Alais ... vs Tilaknagar Ps on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93133471/
3 College and he demanded Rs.38,00,000/- and accordingly they paid Crl.Appeal No.2560/2019 Rs.38,00,000/- to the accused in August 2014 and thereafter in December 2014 they came to know that the admission has not taken place, so they approached the police and filed the complaint.

sentences.text: The accused has not repaid them the money and has not given them the MBBS seat.
Also they have identified the accused before the court through VC.
The learned Magistrate has rightly appreciated the evidence of P.Ws.3 and 4.

There is incriminating material against them and also the prosecution has also placed convincing materials before the court to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt and the accused has been rightly convicted.

15. It is also observed that the accused No.1 is in judicial custody till today in some other case, which is pending before the learned XII ACMM, Hyderabad and also several cases are pending against the accused for the same offences in C.C.No.10832/2015, C.C.No.30400/2015 and C.C.No.20412/2015 of Tilak Nagar Police Station.
The learned Magistrate has observed that on perusal of the order sheet, the accused had obtained statutory bail as per order of the court dated:9.03.2015 and he was produced under body warrant.

Further after the accused being convicted for the offence while hear regarding the sentence, it was submitted by the advocate for accused that the Crl.Appeal No.2560/2019 accused is in judicial custody and sought to give set off for the period during which he is in judicial custody.

While passing the order for sentencing, the learned Magistrate has observed in the judgment that the accused No.1 is in judicial custody in some other case and he is not entitled for set off out of sentence of imprisonment imposed on him for the alleged offences.

16. In this regard it is pertinent to note that during the pendency of the appeal, the counsel for appellant filed memo stating that the appellant has undergone sentence imprisonment of 2 years 12 days.
Hence, submitted that the judgment of the trial court be confirmed and imprisonment already undergone by the appellant/accused be set off and appeal be disposed off accordingly.

Learned Public Prosecutor submitted that he has no objection regarding the confirmation of the order passed by the trial court in C.C.No.30400/2015.
17.

In view of the observation made by the learned Magistrate in C.C.No.30400/2015 and the submission made by the learned advocate for accused in this case, it is necessary to refer to the order sheet in C.C.No.30400/2015 as to whether the accused was in judicial custody or not.

It appears that on 7.07.2018 the court was informed that the accused was in custody Crl.Appeal No.2560/2019 in some other case and UTP No.4954/2018 was furnished by the jurisdictional police and the learned Magistrate has issued body warrant against him and on 13.07.2018 the accused was produced under body warrant.
Hence it can be safely said that the accused was not in judicial custody in this case.

Even otherwise on perusal of the order sheet in Crime No.360/2014 pertaining to C.C.No.30400/2015 it is observed that on 24.02.2015 the Investigating Officer had filed a requisition stating that the accused Santhosh Rai @ Raghav Mishra is in judicial custody in another case and his UTP No.13312/2014 and accordingly body warrant was issued against him.
On 7.03.2015 the accused was produced before the learned Magistrate under body warrant.
On 22.05.2015 the learned Magistrate released the accused by passing orders on application under Section 167(2) of Cr.P.C..
In the said order it is specifically noted that the accused was been produced in this case under body warrant.

Also there is a delay of more than 60 days in filing the Santhosh Rai Alias Santhosh Alais ... vs Tilaknagar Ps on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93133471/
4 charge sheet and the accused is in judicial custody he was enlarged on bail.
18.

sentences.text: But as per the order sheet dated:1.06.2015 to 11.12.2015, the accused was produced under body warrant in crime stage.
After filing of the charge sheet the case came to be registered as C.C.No.30400/2015, NBW was issued.
On 13.07.2018 the accused was Crl.Appeal No.2560/2019 produced under body warrant, but from 26.07.2018 to 2.11.2018 the accused was produced from judicial custody.
On 15.11.2018 it is noted that the accused was not produced from judicial custody as he was taken to Vishakapatnam to attend the case.
In the order sheet from 28.11.2018 to 10.07.2019 it is noted that the accused is produced from judicial custody.

Hence it can be safely said that the accused was in judicial custody from 26.07.2018.
19.

Here itself it is necessary to note that the judicial custody is a custody where person is being kept in prison on the orders of the Magistrate before whom the criminal case against him is pending and in judicial custody the accused becomes the responsibility of the court.

While "body warrant" i.e.,
production warrant is a court order to bring an accused already in custody in another case to another court for production.
The Magistrate in front of whom he is produced under body warrant has no direct custody of the accused.
Hence judicial custody and producing under body warrant are two distinct proceedings and same cannot be overlapped.

In this case from the entries in the order sheet, it appears that the learned Magistrate has taken the judicial custody when he was produced before him whether it is in compliance of procedural of law or not Crl.Appeal No.2560/2019 cannot be looked into by this court at this stage, but taking note that the accused was in judicial custody as stated by the learned advocate for the accused for 2 years 12 days, for which the learned Public Prosecutor has submitted no objection.
20. In view of the discussion mad supra, it is held that the accused has not made out a ground to set aside the conviction judgment passed by the learned Magistrate.
Further appellant/accused has made out a ground to set off for the imprisonment already undergone by him in judicial custody.
Accordingly, the Point No.1 in the Negative and Point No.2 in the Affirmative.
21. POINT No.3 :

In view of my findings on Point Nos.1 and 2 as above, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Crl.
Appeal filed by the appellant is hereby dismissed.
Consequently, the impugned judgment passed by the learned I ACMM, Bengaluru in C.C.No.30400/2015, dated:16.11.2019 stands confirmed.
Further the imprisonment undergone by the accused is given set off.
Crl.Appeal No.2560/2019 Send back the records to the trial court along with the copy of this judgment.
